subject: apush
topic_title: Contextualizing Period 1
learning_objective: Explain the context for European encounters in the Americas from 1491 to 1607.
question: Which statement about the Americas in 1491 is most accurate?

options.A: Large farming societies and cities, such as Tenochtitlan and Cahokia, existed
options.B: The Americas were a sparsely populated wilderness of only nomadic hunter-gatherers
options.C: Native peoples had no political organization beyond small family bands
options.D: Native societies had not yet developed agriculture or trade networks

explanation: Cahokia built massive earthen mounds near the Mississippi, and the Mexica ruled Tenochtitlan, so the wilderness view is a misconception.

distractor_notes.B: Some societies were mobile, but many were not.

trap.trap_description: Students often picture pre-contact America as an empty wilderness.
trap.why_students_fall_for_it: Popular images of discovery suggest empty land, so the nomadic-only option feels familiar.
trap.how_to_avoid: Recall the large cities and mound centers (Tenochtitlan, Cahokia) and the maize-based societies of the period.

subject: apush
topic_title: Contextualizing Period 1
learning_objective: Explain the context for European encounters in the Americas from 1491 to 1607.
question: Which statement about Native societies in North America before European contact is most accurate?

options.A: All of them relied mainly on maize farming for food
options.B: They differed widely in language, economy, and political structure
options.C: None of them lived in large settled communities
options.D: All of them belonged to a single political confederacy

explanation: Northwest Coast peoples centered on salmon, Plains peoples on bison, and Hohokam on irrigated farming, so the all and none statements fail.

distractor_notes.A: Many groups did not rely mainly on maize.
distractor_notes.C: Cahokia and Pueblo communities were large and settled.
distractor_notes.D: No single confederacy united all Native societies.

trap.trap_description: Absolute words such as all and none produce false generalizations about Native diversity.
trap.why_students_fall_for_it: Students who learned about maize cultures may assume all groups farmed the same way.
trap.how_to_avoid: Be suspicious of absolutes and recall contrasting examples: salmon fishing in the Northwest, bison hunting on the Plains, irrigation in the Southwest.

stimulus.content: “a boundary or straight line be determined and drawn north and south, from pole to pole, on the said ocean sea, from the Arctic to the Antarctic pole . . . at a distance of three hundred and seventy leagues west of the Cape Verde Islands . . . by the said King and Queen of Castile, Aragon, etc., and by their vessels, on the western side of the said bound”
stimulus.citation: Treaty of Tordesillas, 1494 (English translation), The Avalon Project, Yale Law School

question: Based only on the excerpt, which statement about the lands west of the line is accurate?

options.A: Lands found by Castile west of the line belong to Castile
options.B: Lands west of the line belong to Portugal
options.C: Lands west of the line belong to the Native peoples who live there
options.D: All lands discovered by Castile anywhere in the world belong to Castile

explanation: The excerpt limits Castile's possession to lands found on the western side of the line; it does not claim lands anywhere or address Native ownership.

distractor_notes.B: The excerpt assigns western lands to Castile.
distractor_notes.D: The excerpt limits Castile's claim to the western side of the line.

trap.trap_description: The question asks what the excerpt says, not what students know generally.
trap.why_students_fall_for_it: A hasty reader sees Castile and forever and expands the claim to all lands anywhere.
trap.how_to_avoid: Locate the exact phrase: on the western side of the said bound.

topic_title: Contextualizing Period 1

question: Which statement is the most complete explanation of why European states explored the Atlantic in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries?

options.B: Economic gain, state competition, and religion all drove exploration
options.C: Exploration was driven mainly by Native Americans inviting Europeans
options.D: The spread of Christianity was the only motive for exploration

trap.how_to_avoid: Prefer answers that combine multiple causes when the question asks for the most complete explanation.

subject: apush
topic_title: Contextualizing Period 1
learning_objective: Explain the context for European encounters in the Americas from 1491 to 1607.
question: A student argues that the 1453 Ottoman capture of Constantinople alone caused Columbus's voyage. Which response best evaluates this claim?

options.A: It is incorrect, because the Ottomans had no effect on European trade
options.B: It is correct, because the Ottomans controlled all of Spain in 1492
options.C: It contributed to the search for routes, but other causes also mattered
options.D: It is correct, because Columbus sailed immediately after the city fell

explanation: The capture of Constantinople is part of the context, but the voyage also depended on Reconquista politics, Portuguese expertise, and royal sponsorship. Columbus sailed in 1492, not 1453.

distractor_notes.A: Ottoman power did affect trade routes.

trap.trap_description: A real background event is treated as the sole cause of a later event.
trap.why_students_fall_for_it: Students link famous events in sequence and assume the earlier one explains the later one.
trap.how_to_avoid: Check the timing and look for additional causes; 1453 and 1492 are nearly four decades apart.

subject: apush
topic_title: Native American Societies Before European Contact
learning_objective: Explain how and why various native populations in the period before European contact interacted with the natural environment in North America.
question: Which statement about Cahokia's decline is most accurate?

options.A: It declined before European contact, so Europeans were not the cause
options.B: Spanish soldiers destroyed it during the conquest of the Aztec Empire in 1521
options.C: Smallpox brought by Columbus's crews emptied the city in 1493
options.D: Its people left after the founding of St. Augustine

explanation: Cahokia's population fell and the site was largely abandoned by the 1300s, before sustained European contact. Later epidemics affected many peoples, but not Cahokia's earlier decline.

distractor_notes.B: The conquest of Mexico occurred in 1519-1521, far to the south.
distractor_notes.C: Columbus did not bring smallpox in 1493.

trap.trap_description: A major decline is wrongly linked to the famous arrival of Europeans.
trap.why_students_fall_for_it: Students associate every Native population decline with European diseases and conquest.
trap.how_to_avoid: Check the dates: Cahokia was largely abandoned by about 1350, long before 1492.

subject: apush
topic_title: Native American Societies Before European Contact
learning_objective: Explain how and why various native populations in the period before European contact interacted with the natural environment in North America.
question: Which statement is the most complete explanation of why Native societies differed so much across North America?

options.A: Their economies differed because Europeans taught them different crops after arriving
options.B: Environment, resources, and history all shaped their economies and politics
options.C: They differed only because they spoke different languages and had different names
options.D: Environment alone determined every aspect of Native life

question: Which statement about the naming of the Americas is accurate?

options.A: Christopher Columbus chose the name America for the lands he reached
options.B: Queen Isabella ordered that the continent be named for her family
options.C: A German mapmaker used the name America in honor of Amerigo Vespucci

options.B: Henry Hudson, who explored the Hudson River
options.C: Samuel de Champlain, who founded Quebec
options.D: John Cabot, who sailed for England in 1497

explanation: Cartier sailed up the St. Lawrence in the 1530s for France. Cabot was English, Hudson explored in 1609, and Champlain founded Quebec in 1608.

trap.trap_description: Several early explorers of northern North America had similar roles.
trap.why_students_fall_for_it: Cabot, Hudson, and Champlain are all linked to northern waters, so students mix them up.
trap.how_to_avoid: Match each explorer to a river or region and a date.

subject: apush
topic_title: European Exploration in the Americas
learning_objective: Explain the causes of exploration and conquest of the New World by various European nations.

stimulus.content:
England, Spain, and Roanoke (author-prepared timeline)
| Year | Event |
| 1584 | Queen Elizabeth I grants Walter Raleigh a patent to explore and settle lands “not actually possessed of any Christian Prince” |
| 1585 | English settlers establish a colony on Roanoke Island |
| 1587 | John White leads a second group of colonists to Roanoke |
| 1588 | England defeats the Spanish Armada |
| 1590 | White returns to Roanoke and finds the colony deserted |
stimulus.citation: Author-prepared timeline based on Avalon Project (Charter to Raleigh) and Wikipedia articles on Roanoke Colony and the Spanish Armada (CC BY-SA)

question: A student claims that England's 1588 defeat of the Spanish Armada caused the disappearance of the Roanoke colonists. Which response is best?

options.A: The claim is correct because Spain's navy destroyed Roanoke after 1588
options.B: The timeline shows the events were related in time, but it does not show that one caused the other
options.C: The claim is incorrect because Roanoke was founded after the Armada's defeat
options.D: The claim is correct because the Armada's defeat left the colony without supplies from Spain

explanation: The timeline lists the Armada's defeat in 1588 and White's return in 1590, but it gives no evidence the Armada caused the colony's disappearance. Roanoke was founded before 1588 and England, not Spain, supplied it.

distractor_notes.A: No source shows Spain destroyed Roanoke.

trap.trap_description: Two events occur close together in the timeline.
trap.why_students_fall_for_it: Because the events are near each other in time, students assume one caused the other.
trap.how_to_avoid: Ask whether the source shows a causal link or only the order of events.

question: A student notes that the Native population of Spanish America fell as the encomienda and the mita expanded, and concludes that these labor systems were the only cause of the decline. Which response is best?

options.A: The conclusion is correct because the population decline began only after 1600
options.B: Labor mattered, but disease was also a major cause, so the claim is too narrow
options.C: The conclusion is wrong because the labor systems had no effect on Native deaths

learning_objective: Explain how and why European and Native American perspectives of others developed and changed in the period.
question: Which person is correctly matched with their role in early Spanish exploration?

options.A: Cabeza de Vaca guided a 1539 expedition toward Zuni; Esteban founded St. Augustine
options.B: Esteban conquered the Aztecs; Cabeza de Vaca conquered the Inca
options.C: Esteban guided a 1539 expedition toward Zuni; Cabeza de Vaca wrote of his travels
options.D: Cabeza de Vaca led the French at Fort Caroline; Esteban led the English at Roanoke

explanation: Esteban guided Fray Marcos de Niza in 1539, while Cabeza de Vaca wrote about his travels.

distractor_notes.B: Cortés and Pizarro conquered the empires.
distractor_notes.D: Fort Caroline was French and Roanoke was English.

trap.trap_description: Two survivors of the same expedition have similar stories.
trap.why_students_fall_for_it: Both men are linked to the Narváez expedition, so students swap them.
trap.how_to_avoid: Link Esteban to Fray Marcos and Zuni, and Cabeza de Vaca to his written account.

options.C: Tiguex War, Guadalupe apparition, Acoma attack
options.D: Guadalupe apparition (1531), Tiguex War (1540–41), Acoma attack (1599)

subject: apush
topic_title: Cultural Interactions Between Europeans, Native Americans, and Africans
learning_objective: Explain how and why European and Native American perspectives of others developed and changed in the period.
question: Which of the following was NOT a cultural effect of Spanish colonization on Native peoples?

options.A: The end of all Indigenous languages
options.B: The development of mestizo communities in New Spain
options.C: The blending of religious festivals
options.D: The spread of Catholic missions and practices

explanation: Many Indigenous languages and customs survived and blended with Spanish ones. Missions, mestizo communities, and blended festivals were effects.

trap.trap_description: A NOT question requires finding the claim that is false.
trap.why_students_fall_for_it: Students choose a familiar effect and ignore the reversal.
trap.how_to_avoid: Underline NOT and eliminate the three true effects.

subject: apush
topic_title: Cultural Interactions Between Europeans, Native Americans, and Africans
learning_objective: Explain how and why European and Native American perspectives of others developed and changed in the period.
question: A student argues that because many Native people attended Catholic services, they must have abandoned all older beliefs. Which response is best?

options.A: The claim is correct because Native peoples had no religion before Spain
options.B: Attendance alone does not show that older beliefs ended; many blended practices
options.C: The claim is incorrect because Native people never attended church
options.D: The claim is correct because Spain forced a complete break with all older beliefs

explanation: Syncretism shows that people often combined practices, so church attendance alone does not prove they abandoned older beliefs.

distractor_notes.D: Spain did not erase all beliefs.

trap.trap_description: One observed behavior is taken as proof of a complete change in belief.
trap.why_students_fall_for_it: Students treat participation as evidence of full conversion.
trap.how_to_avoid: Ask whether the evidence shows a single cause or only a related change.

topic_title: Cultural Interactions Between Europeans, Native Americans, and Africans
learning_objective: Explain how and why European and Native American perspectives of others developed and changed in the period.

stimulus.content: Describing Hernando de Soto's demand on a Native leader in the Southeast (1540): “At the time of his departure, by the importunity of some, which would have more than was reason, he demanded of the cacique thirty women to make slaves of. He answered that he would confer with his chief men. And before he returned an answer, one night all of them with their wives and children forsook the town, and fled away”
stimulus.citation: A Gentleman of Elvas, True Relation of the Hardships Suffered by Governor Fernando de Soto (published 1557), Hakluyt's 1609 English translation, Project Gutenberg #34997

question: In the passage, what did De Soto demand from the Native leader?

options.A: Thirty baskets of corn for the journey
options.B: Thirty guides to lead him to the sea
options.C: Thirty women to make slaves of
options.D: Thirty warriors to join his army

explanation: The text says De Soto demanded thirty women to make slaves of.

trap.trap_description: The options use the same number with different demands.
trap.why_students_fall_for_it: Students remember the number thirty but not what was demanded.
trap.how_to_avoid: Reread the exact demand in the passage.

subject: apush
topic_title: Causation in Period 1
learning_objective: Explain the effects of the development of transatlantic voyages from 1491 to 1607.
question: Which statement correctly distinguishes the Treaty of Alcáçovas (1479) from the Treaty of Tordesillas (1494)?

options.A: Alcáçovas divided the Americas; Tordesillas settled claims about Africa
options.B: Both treaties divided North America between England and Spain
options.C: Alcáçovas settled claims about Africa and the Atlantic islands; Tordesillas divided newly found lands west of Africa
options.D: Alcáçovas created the Spanish treasure fleets; Tordesillas created the encomienda

explanation: Alcáçovas recognized Portuguese rights in Guinea and left the Canary Islands to Castile. Tordesillas drew a line that gave Portugal Brazil and Spain most of the rest of the Americas.

trap.trap_description: Two treaties between Spain and Portugal are often confused.
trap.why_students_fall_for_it: Both involve Spain and Portugal and the Atlantic, so students swap them.
trap.how_to_avoid: Link Alcáçovas to 1479 and the African coast, Tordesillas to 1494 and a line west of Cape Verde.

subject: apush
topic_title: Causation in Period 1
learning_objective: Explain the effects of the development of transatlantic voyages from 1491 to 1607.
question: A student writes, 'Columbus sailed in 1492 because Constantinople fell in 1453.' Which response is best?

options.A: The claim is correct because the Ottoman capture was the only cause of European exploration
options.B: The claim is correct because Constantinople's fall forced Spain to explore
options.C: The claim is incorrect because the Ottoman Empire had no effect on trade
options.D: The Ottoman capture was one factor, but Portuguese competition, Spanish unification, and navigation advances also mattered

explanation: Ottoman power influenced trade, but many factors, including Spanish ambition and Portuguese models, led to Columbus's voyage.

distractor_notes.A: It was not the only cause.

trap.trap_description: One earlier event is treated as the sole cause of a later one.
trap.why_students_fall_for_it: Dates show an order, so students assume a direct and only cause.
trap.how_to_avoid: Look for multiple causes and avoid a single-cause explanation.

question: Which statement about the effects of the voyages is most accurate?

options.A: They brought benefits to Native peoples and Europeans equally
options.B: They brought wealth to some Europeans and caused severe population loss for many Native peoples
options.C: They harmed Europeans while benefiting Native peoples
options.D: They had little effect on any society

explanation: The voyages enriched some Europeans and brought disease and forced labor to many Native peoples.

trap.trap_description: Each wrong option oversimplifies the effects.
trap.why_students_fall_for_it: Students remember benefits for Europe and ignore Native losses, or the reverse.
trap.how_to_avoid: Check for effects on each group before choosing.

question: A student writes, 'Spain conquered the Americas only because it had better technology than Native peoples.' Which response best evaluates the claim?

options.A: It is accurate because Spain always outnumbered Native armies
options.B: It is inaccurate because technology played no role
options.C: It oversimplifies, since disease, Native allies, and political divisions also mattered
options.D: It is accurate because Native peoples had no weapons

explanation: Weapons and horses mattered, but disease and Native alliances were also important.

trap.trap_description: The word only reduces a complex process to one cause.
trap.why_students_fall_for_it: Technology was important, so students accept the absolute claim.
trap.how_to_avoid: Watch for the word only and test whether other causes are documented.

question: Which of the following was NOT an effect of European voyages to the Americas?

options.A: The growth of the Atlantic slave trade
options.B: Increased rivalry among European powers
options.C: The movement of crops and animals across the Atlantic
options.D: The disappearance of all Native societies by 1600

explanation: Native societies lost population and land but did not disappear by 1600. The other three were effects.

trap.how_to_avoid: Underline NOT and eliminate the three true effects.

stimulus.content: [Described map, author-prepared] A map of the Atlantic Ocean shows a vertical line labeled “Line of 1494,” drawn 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde Islands. The area west of the line is labeled “Castile.” The area east of the line is labeled “Portugal.” The easternmost bulge of South America lies east of the line.
stimulus.citation: Author-prepared description of the demarcation set by the Treaty of Tordesillas (1494), based on Avalon Project and Wikipedia (CC BY-SA)

question: According to the map, which area was labeled Castile?

options.A: The area west of the line
options.B: The eastern bulge of South America
options.C: The Cape Verde Islands
options.D: The area east of the line

explanation: The map labels the area west of the line Castile and the area east of the line Portugal.

distractor_notes.B: The bulge lies east of the line.
distractor_notes.C: The islands mark the starting point.

trap.trap_description: East and west can be reversed when reading a map.
trap.why_students_fall_for_it: Students see Brazil on the east and assume Castile is there.
trap.how_to_avoid: Read the labels and directions carefully.

subject: apush
topic_title: Causation in Period 1
learning_objective: Explain the effects of the development of transatlantic voyages from 1491 to 1607.
question: Which statement about silver from the Americas is most accurate?

options.A: It ended Spanish interest in the Americas
options.B: It enriched Spain and also contributed to rising prices across Europe
options.C: It reduced prices throughout Europe
options.D: It made Spain poorer because silver had no value

explanation: Silver increased Spain's money supply and was linked to inflation.

trap.trap_description: Students assume wealth from the colonies only helped Spain.
trap.why_students_fall_for_it: Treasure sounds purely beneficial, so effects such as inflation are missed.
trap.how_to_avoid: Consider both the gains and the economic side effects.
